lesson_title: Distance vs Displacement: The Odometer and the Pigeon
hook_text: Run a full 400 m lap and physics says you went... nowhere. Here's why that's correct.
clip_script: Two ways to measure a journey. The odometer counts every metre the wheels roll — that is distance: ground covered, direction ignored. The pigeon does not care about your route: released at the finish, it flies straight back to the start, and that flight is displacement — start to finish, direction included. Walk 40 metres east, then 30 back west: odometer says 70, pigeon flies just 10, pointing at a displacement of 10 metres east. Now the extreme: run a full lap of the track. Odometer: 400 metres, proudly. The pigeon does not even take off — start and finish are the same spot. Displacement zero. Effort is real; net change is nothing. Two instruments, two honest answers.
visual_style: Split screen: a ticking odometer racking up metres versus a pigeon on a straight dotted line; the lap ends with the odometer at 400 while the pigeon shrugs on its perch.
mood: Playful paradox resolved with a grin.
pacing: Hook with the zero claim, quick dual-instrument setup, lap punchline landing on the sleeping pigeon.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and split speed from velocity the same way.
